dedupe_keys.name: global mining in socially vulnerable areas wri 2003

description: This dataset maps the social vulnerability of areas around the world where mining takes place, measured as a function of adult literacy, functional literacy and income. It was developed by the World Resources Institute for its Mining and Critical Ecosystems project and published in 2003, using data from Barro and Lee (2002), Oxfam America (2001) and the World Bank (2003), and was uploaded to the Data Basin platform of the Conservation Biology Institute on 7 July 2010. Coverage is global; the metadata do not give a content date or spatial resolution. The layer is available online and can be viewed and mapped free on Data Basin, with full FGDC metadata; WRI's use constraints say it is not for use in litigation and carry no warranty of accuracy, and no open licence is stated. Caveats: the indicators date from around 2000, the combination method is described only briefly, and the original WRI link in the metadata is old. For simulation it gives a baseline layer of social vulnerability to overlay with mine locations and hazard maps when assessing which mining regions have communities least able to cope with accidents, tailings failures or supply shocks. It is related to the WRI mining concessions record in this catalogue, another WRI mining layer.
